jurisdictions.name: Lexington / Fayette County
jurisdictions.office: Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government, Division of Building Inspection
notes: An in-ground pool needs a Swimming Pool Permit from the Division of Building Inspection. Fayette County Health Department approval is also required before the permit is issued.
The online application needs a site plan showing lot, fence, easements, existing structures, the proposed pool, walkways and distances to property lines, plus a subdivision plat or mortgage survey.
The fence must be shown on the site plan: at least 4 ft high, no openings over 4 inches, with self-closing, self-latching gates that open outward.
Residential pools are regulated under the 2018 Kentucky Residential Code. Easements need encroachment agreements, and floodplain sites need a special permit from the Division of Engineering.

sources.title: Permit Guide For Swimming Pools (Lexington Building Inspection, 2026)

jurisdictions.name: Warren County
jurisdictions.office: Warren County Public Works, Building Services
notes: Warren County says all swimming pools, above-ground and in-ground, need a building permit, and every pool needs a barrier.
A pool permit application must include a set of building plans and a professionally drawn plot plan.
Since September 15, 2026, in-ground pool applications also need a detailed pool layout showing items such as the electrical panel, equipment, ladders, lights, depth and fence.
The county says applications without a detailed plan will not be accepted, and final inspections of pools are required.

sources.title: Requirements for all inground swimming pool building permit applications (memo, 15 Sept 2026)

jurisdictions.name: Boone County
notes: Boone County's pool application needs a plot plan approved by the Boone County Planning Commission, plus the contractor's county occupational license.
The pool enclosure drawing must show fence type, height and openings, and comply with section R326.8 of the 2018 Kentucky Residential Code.
Applicants must submit a pool layout and cross section with water depths, plus circulation plans meeting ANSI/NSPI-5 2003 and ANSI/APSP-7 2006 suction entrapment standards.
Electrical work needs an electrical permit from the county's third-party electrical inspection agency, and retaining walls built with the pool need a separate permit.

sources.title: Acknowledgment of Residential swimming pool/hot tub requirements (Boone County Building Department)

jurisdictions.name: Covington
jurisdictions.office: City of Covington Department of Development, Zoning
notes: Covington handles pools through a zoning permit application, with the pool checked under Site Improvements, and it asks for current exterior photos and a site plan.
No pool may sit forward of the principal structure or in the front yard of any lot.
Pools need a fence or wall four to six feet high with self-closing or self-latching gates, and openings may not pass a four-inch sphere.
Water from a non-public source must be approved by the Northern Kentucky District Health Department.

sources.title: Applying for a Zoning Permit - Pools (City of Covington)
